title: One reading advance
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input and let $c$ be a configuration with $m$ work tapes. Suppose $r$ and $s$ are distinct tape indices, tape $r$ of $c$ contains the binary representation of $i$, and the head on tape $r$ is at position $0$. If $k<\min(i,|x|)$, then there is a number $T$ such that the reading program, started in its initial reading phase with tape $s$ holding the binary representation of $k$ and the input head at position $k+1$, reaches the same initial reading phase with tape $s$ holding the binary representation of $k+1$ and the input head at position $k+2$. Every configuration at a time $n<T$ lies in the read frame of $c$.
